files.name: aisk-check-arch
files.description: Use when the user wants to check whether code changes align with recorded architecture decisions.

files.name: aisk-complete-task
files.description: Use when the user wants to verify task completion, clean up task documents, and prepare a pull request.

files.name: aisk-create-task
files.description: Use when the user wants to initialize a new development task with branch setup, task documents, and work mode.

files.name: aisk-create-walkthrough
files.description: Use when the user wants to create a new walkthrough of code changes at a specific version or commit range.

files.name: aisk-init-project
files.description: Use when the user wants to configure a new project to work with globally installed aisk skills, setting up .gitignore and the .ai-skills directory.

files.name: aisk-refresh-arch
files.description: Use when the user wants to scan a codebase and generate or refresh architecture decision notes.

files.name: aisk-resume-task
files.description: Use when the user wants to resume task work mode — identical behavior to start-task.

files.name: aisk-resume-walkthrough
files.description: Use when the user wants to resume a walkthrough — identical behavior to start-walkthrough.

files.name: aisk-setup-precommit
files.description: Use when the user wants to configure a Node.js project pre-commit hook with lint-staged.

files.name: aisk-smart-review
files.description: Use when the user asks for iterative review and fixes within a specified file, module, or directory.

files.name: aisk-start-task
files.description: Use when the user wants to enter task work mode and load context for the current task.

files.name: aisk-start-walkthrough
files.description: Use when the user wants to resume a walkthrough from the saved state in a new session.

files.name: aisk-verify-step
files.description: Use when the user wants to run acceptance checks for a single implementation step.

files.name: aisk-verify-task
files.description: Use when the user wants to run acceptance checks across all steps of the current task.
